audit_items.proof_trace: get_price_with_check divides the absolute price difference by spot_price_value in both branches (L51, L53), rather than ema_price_value as the property specifies. When spot > EMA (the flash-loan inflation direction), the formula `(spot-ema)/spot` is systematically more lenient than `(spot-ema)/ema`; with the 10% default tolerance the effective allowed spot deviation becomes ~11.1% instead of 10%, allowing borrow/withdraw operations in oracle states that the circuit breaker was designed to block. The function correctly returns ema_price_value for actual valuations, so direct price-manipulation theft is not possible, but the weaker gate is a real security reduction.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An attacker flash-loans to inflate the spot price of a collateral or debt asset to ~10.5% above its EMA. The code formula yields `(10.5%)/(110.5%) ≈ 9.5%`, which passes the 10% tolerance check, so is_obligation_safe proceeds using the correct EMA price; while valuations remain EMA-based, the protocol operates in a manipulated oracle state that the property mandates should be blocked, leaving a residual window for coordinated attacks during elevated market volatility.
